original_summary: On a chilly, rainy night in New York, a patrolman on his beat finds a man waiting in the dark doorway of a closed hardware store. The man explains that twenty years ago he and his best friend Jimmy Wells dined at 'Big Joe' Brady's restaurant on this spot and promised to meet here again exactly twenty years later, at ten o'clock, whatever their fortunes. He has come a thousand miles from the West, where he has grown rich, and he will wait half an hour. The patrolman says goodnight and walks on. About twenty minutes later a tall man in a long overcoat hurries over and greets him as Bob; they walk arm in arm until a bright drugstore window lights both faces, and Bob sees that this is not Jimmy. The man tells him he has been under arrest for ten minutes as 'Silky' Bob, wanted in Chicago, and hands him a note from Patrolman Wells: Jimmy was on time, recognized the wanted man when the match lit the cigar, and could not arrest his old friend himself, so he sent a plain clothes man to do it.
seed_elements: A man waits in the dark doorway of a closed hardware store on a cold, drizzly night, with an unlit cigar, and explains to a passing patrolman that he is keeping a promise made twenty years ago: to meet his best friend on this exact spot at ten o'clock, whatever their fortunes.

The restaurant where they said goodbye is gone; the man tells how the two young men grew up together like brothers, how he left for the West to make his fortune while his friend refused to leave New York, and how they lost touch; he is proud, a little boastful about his success, and sure his friend will come.

The patrolman listens calmly, asks a few friendly questions, learns the man will wait half an hour, wishes him luck and walks on along his beat; the details (a pale square-jawed face, a small scar near the eyebrow, a large diamond scarfpin) are noticed in the match light.

About twenty minutes later a tall man in a long overcoat, collar turned up, hurries over and says 'Is that you, Bob?'; the waiting man joyfully answers 'Jimmy Wells!', and the two walk off arm in arm while the man from the West starts to tell his story.

Under the bright light of a drugstore the man from the West stops: this tall man's nose is not Jimmy's ('not long enough to change a man's nose from a Roman to a pug'); the tall man says it sometimes changes a good man into a bad one, and that Bob has been under arrest for ten minutes as 'Silky' Bob, wanted by Chicago.

He hands over a short note from Patrolman Wells: Jimmy was there on time, saw by the match light that it was the man wanted in Chicago, could not do it himself, and so got a plain clothes man to do the job; the story ends with the note, signed JIMMY.
discarded_elements: Most of the street description (the wind, the lights of cigar stores and lunch counters, the officer twirling his club)
The bragging details (the diamond-set watch, 'razor-edge' of the West, 'Bully' as an answer), if space is needed
Names of minor places and people other than the two friends (the restaurant owner's name, the city department), if a shorter version works better
Most of the small talk between the patrolman and the waiting man, and the rain and wind descriptions between scenes
conversion_plan: Keep the New York street setting at night and the original order of events; do not modernize the setting. Write it mainly in natural third-person English at about 400 words, with the waiting man (Bob) as the main character, the patrolman on the beat and the tall man in the overcoat described by roles (the patrolman, the tall man) and Jimmy mentioned by name only as Bob's old friend. Preserve the central story, the relationship between the two friends, the cause-and-effect chain and the ending: the twenty-year promise told to the patrolman; the patrolman's calm, friendly manner and his walking on; the tall man's greeting and the warm walk arm in arm; the discovery under the drugstore light that this is not Jimmy; the arrest of the wanted man; and the note from Patrolman Wells, which is the original's closing reveal. Keep the quiet suspense and the bittersweet twist: Jimmy kept the promise and also did his duty. Do not explain the trick, hint that the patrolman is Jimmy, or comment on the twist before the note, and do not add a moral or an explanation of your own after the note. The note itself is not such an explanation: it is the closing line of the story and must be kept; the surprise is the point. Compress by trimming the street description, the boasting and the small talk, not by cutting the foreshadowing in the patrolman's conversation with Bob.

title: 二十年後 After Twenty Years (O. Henry)

ending_reveal.meaning: The story ends with the note from Patrolman Wells, which reveals that the patrolman Bob spoke with at the start was Jimmy himself: Jimmy kept the promise and came on time, recognized Bob as the man wanted in Chicago, and could not arrest his old friend, so he had a plain clothes man do it.
ending_reveal.source_quote: Somehow I couldn't do it myself, so I went around and got a plain clothes man to do the job.
ending_reveal.withhold_until_end: Before the note, do not hint that the patrolman is Jimmy, that Bob is a wanted man, or that the tall man is not Jimmy.

setups_and_payoffs.setup: Bob tells the patrolman about the twenty-year promise with his best friend Jimmy and says he will wait half an hour; the patrolman listens calmly and walks on.
setups_and_payoffs.payoff: The tall man who comes at the half-hour mark pretends to be Jimmy; under the drugstore light Bob sees it is not Jimmy, and he is arrested as the man wanted in Chicago.

key_roles.name: Bob
key_roles.role: the man from the West who waits in the doorway, keeps the twenty-year promise and is arrested

key_roles.name: Jimmy
key_roles.role: Bob's best friend and the other half of the promise, who turns out to be the patrolman
the patrolman on the beat who talks with Bob and walks on (he is Jimmy, but this is revealed only by the final note)
the tall man in the long overcoat, a plain clothes officer who pretends to be Jimmy and arrests Bob

key_causality: Jimmy comes to keep the promise and, by the light of the match, recognizes Bob as the man wanted in Chicago; unable to arrest his friend himself, he has a plain clothes man pose as Jimmy and make the arrest, and leaves a note for Bob.
free_to_cut: the street and weather description, Bob's boasting about his success, the details of their years apart, and most of the small talk between the patrolman and Bob
